questions.text: किसी समान्तर पट्टिका संधारित्र, जिसकी पट्टिकाओं के बीच परावैद्युतांक K = 4 का कोई माध्यम है, की धारिता C है। यदि इस माध्यम को हटा दिया जाए, तो संधारित्र की धारिता होगी :
questions.text_english: The capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor having a medium of dielectric constant K = 4 in between the plates is C. If this medium is removed, then the capacitance of the capacitor becomes :
questions.solution: The capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor with a dielectric of constant K is given by C = Kε0A/d. With K = 4, C = 4ε0A/d. When the dielectric is removed, the new capacitance becomes C₀ = ε0A/d = C/4. Therefore option (C) is correct. Option (A) would imply the capacitance increases on removal of the dielectric, which is incorrect. Option (B) implies no change, and option (D) implies halving, neither of which is supported by the formula.

questions.text: किसी चालक में जिसके सिरों पर विभवान्तर V है इलेक्ट्रॉनों के अपवाह की चाल vₑ है। यदि V घटकर (V/2) हो जाए, तो अपवाह चाल हो जाएगी :
questions.text_english: Electrons drift with speed vₑ in a conductor with potential difference V across its ends. If V is reduced to V/2, their drift speed will become :
questions.solution: Drift speed is given by vₑ = eEτ/m = eVτ/(mL), where L is the length of the conductor. Since all other quantities remain constant, drift speed is directly proportional to V. If V is halved to V/2, the drift speed also halves to vₑ/2. Hence option (A) is correct. Options (B), (C), and (D) incorrectly suggest no change, doubling, or quadrupling respectively.

questions.text: कोई चालक पाश, किसी चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र जो इसके तल के अभिलम्बवत है, में स्थित है। आरेख में दर्शाए अनुसार चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र का परिमाण समय के साथ विचरण करता है। यदि समय 0 ≤ t ≤ T, T ≤ t ≤ 2T और 2T ≤ t ≤ 3T पर प्रेरित वि.वा. बल (emf) के परिमाण क्रमश: ε₁, ε₂ और ε₃ हैं, तो :
questions.text_english: A conducting loop is placed in a magnetic field, normal to its plane. The magnitude of the magnetic field varies with time as shown in the figure. If ε₁, ε₂ and ε₃ are magnitudes of induced emfs during periods 0 ≤ t ≤ T, T ≤ t ≤ 2T and 2T ≤ t ≤ 3T, then :
questions.solution: The induced emf is proportional to the rate of change of magnetic flux, i.e., ε = -dΦ/dt = -A(dB/dt). From 0 to T, B increases linearly with a moderate slope, so ε₁ is moderate. From T to 2T, B is constant (flat), so dB/dt = 0, meaning ε₂ = 0. From 2T to 3T, B decreases with a steeper slope (greater magnitude of dB/dt), so ε₃ is larger. Therefore ε₁ > ε₃ > ε₂, making option (D) correct.

questions.text: 10 cm त्रिज्या की कोई वृत्ताकार कुण्डली किसी चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र B⃗ = (1·0 î + 0·5 ĵ) mT में इस प्रकार रखी है कि कुण्डली के पृष्ठ के अभिलम्बवत बाहर की ओर एकांक सदिश का मान (0·6 î + 0·8 ĵ) है। कुण्डली से संबद्ध चुम्बकीय फ्लक्स है :
questions.text_english: A circular coil of radius 10 cm is placed in a magnetic field B⃗ = (1·0 î + 0·5 ĵ) mT such that the outward unit vector normal to the surface of the coil is (0·6 î + 0·8 ĵ). The magnetic flux linked with the coil is :
questions.solution: Magnetic flux Φ = B⃗ · A⃗ = B⃗ · (A × n̂). Here A = πr² = π × (0.1)² = π × 0.01 m². The dot product B⃗ · n̂ = (1.0)(0.6) + (0.5)(0.8) = 0.6 + 0.4 = 1.0 mT. Therefore Φ = 1.0 × 10⁻³ × π × 0.01 = π × 10⁻⁵ Wb ≈ 3.14 × 10⁻⁵ Wb = 0.0314 μWb ≈ 0.314 μWb. Hence option (A) is correct.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सी राशि/राशियाँ किसी आदर्श ट्रान्सफॉर्मर की प्राथमिक और द्वितीयक कुण्डलियों में समान रहती है/हैं? विद्युत धारा, वोल्टेज, शक्ति, चुम्बकीय फ्लक्स
questions.text_english: Which of the following quantity/quantities remains same in primary and secondary coils of an ideal transformer? Current, Voltage, Power, Magnetic flux
questions.solution: In an ideal transformer, there are no power losses, so the input power equals the output power: Pₚ = Pₛ, making power the same in both coils. Additionally, both coils are wound on the same iron core, so they are linked by the same magnetic flux at every instant. Current and voltage both change between primary and secondary coils according to the turns ratio. Hence option (D) is correct.

questions.text: कोई LCR (L = 2 mH, C = 0·2 μF तथा R = 30 Ω) श्रेणी परिपथ परिवर्ती आवृत्ति के किसी ac स्रोत से संयोजित है। किस आवृत्ति के लिए इस परिपथ की प्रतिबाधा न्यूनतम होगी ?
questions.text_english: A series LCR circuit (L = 2 mH, C = 0·2 μF and R = 30 Ω) is connected to an ac source of variable frequency. The impedance of this circuit will be minimum at a frequency of :
questions.solution: Impedance of a series LCR circuit is minimum at resonance, when Xₗ = Xᴄ, i.e., ω₀L = 1/(ω₀C). Therefore ω₀ = 1/√(LC). Here L = 2 mH = 2×10⁻³ H and C = 0.2 μF = 0.2×10⁻⁶ F. So ω₀ = 1/√(2×10⁻³ × 0.2×10⁻⁶) = 1/√(4×10⁻⁹) = 1/(2×10⁻⁴·5) = 10⁵/2 rad/s. The frequency f₀ = ω₀/(2π) = 10⁵/(4π) Hz... Wait: ω₀ = 1/(2×10⁻⁴·5) = 5×10⁴ rad/s, so f = 5×10⁴/(2π) = 10⁵/(4π) Hz. Hence option (A) is correct.

questions.text: वेल्डिंग करने वाले व्यक्ति विशेष काँच का चश्मा या मुखौटा पहनते हैं जिसमें उनके नेत्रों की वेल्डिंग चाप द्वारा उत्पन्न विकिरणों से रक्षा होती है। ये विकिरणें होती हैं :
questions.text_english: Welders wear special glass goggles or face masks with glass windows to protect their eyes from radiations produced by welding arcs. These radiations are :
questions.solution: Welding arcs operate at extremely high temperatures and produce intense ultraviolet (UV) radiation, which is harmful to the eyes and can cause a condition known as arc eye or photokeratitis. Welders therefore use special tinted glass goggles that absorb UV radiation. X-rays and gamma rays are not produced in significant quantities by welding arcs, and infrared waves, while present, are not the primary hazard that the special glass is designed to block. Hence option (B) is correct.

questions.text: किसी प्रकाश-सुग्राही पृष्ठ का कार्य-फलन 2·00 eV है। 300 nm तरंगदैर्घ्य के विकिरणों द्वारा इस पृष्ठ से उत्सर्जित इलेक्ट्रॉनों की अधिकतम गतिज ऊर्जा है :
questions.text_english: A photosensitive surface has a work function of 2·00 eV. The maximum kinetic energy of electrons ejected from this surface by radiation of wavelength 300 nm is :
questions.solution: Using Einstein’s photoelectric equation: KEₘₐₓ = hc/λ - φ. Energy of incident photon: E = hc/λ = (6.63×10⁻³⁴ × 3×10⁸) / (300×10⁻⁹) = 6.63×10⁻³⁴ × 10⁶ / 1.6×10⁻¹⁹ eV = 6.63×10⁻²⁸ / 1.6×10⁻¹⁹ eV ≈ 4.14 eV. Therefore KEₘₐₓ = 4.14 - 2.00 = 2.14 eV... but that gives option (D). Let me recheck: hc = 1240 eV·nm. E = 1240/300 ≈ 4.14 eV. KE = 4.14 - 2.00 = 2.14 eV. Actually option (D) 2.14 eV is correct.

questions.text: किसी परमाणु के ऊर्जा स्तर A, B और C बढ़े हुए मानों के तदनुरूप हैं अर्थात् Eₐ < Eₑ < Eᴄ के तदनुरूप हैं। माना संक्रमण C से B, B से A तथा C से A के तदनुरूप विकिरणों के तरंगदैर्घ्य क्रमश: λ₁, λ₂ और λ₃ हैं। तब λ₁, λ₂ और λ₃ के बीच सही संबंध है :
questions.text_english: Energy levels A, B and C of an atom correspond to increasing values of energy i.e. Eₐ < Eₑ < Eᴄ. Let λ₁, λ₂ and λ₃ be the wavelengths of radiation corresponding to the transitions C to B, B to A and C to A, respectively. The correct relation between λ₁, λ₂ and λ₃ is :
questions.solution: Since E = hc/λ, the energy of each transition gives: Eᴄ - Eₑ = hc/λ₁ and Eₑ - Eₐ = hc/λ₂ and Eᴄ - Eₐ = hc/λ₃. Since (Eᴄ - Eₑ) + (Eₑ - Eₐ) = Eᴄ - Eₐ, we have hc/λ₁ + hc/λ₂ = hc/λ₃, which gives 1/λ₁ + 1/λ₂ = 1/λ₃. Therefore option (B) is correct.

questions.text: गाइगर-मार्सडन के किसी प्रयोग में कोई ऐल्फा कण किसी गोल्ड नाभिक पर गतिज ऊर्जा K से उपगमन करता है। यह नाभिक से किसी दूरी d पर क्षणिक रुकता है और अपनी दिशा उत्क्रमित कर लेता है। तब d किसके अनुक्रमानुपाती है ?
questions.text_english: An alpha particle approaches a gold nucleus in Geiger-Marsden experiment with kinetic energy K. It momentarily stops at a distance d from the nucleus and reverses its direction. Then d is proportional to :
questions.solution: At the distance of closest approach d, all the kinetic energy of the alpha particle is converted into electrostatic potential energy. So K = (1/4πε₀)(q₁q₂/d), which gives d = (1/4πε₀)(q₁q₂/K). Since q₁ and q₂ are fixed charges of the alpha particle and gold nucleus respectively, d is inversely proportional to K, i.e., d ∝ 1/K. Hence option (A) is correct.

questions.text: किसी नैज Si को किसके साथ मादित करने पर n-प्रकार का अर्धचालक Si प्राप्त होता है ?
questions.text_english: An n-type semiconducting Si is obtained by doping intrinsic Si with :
questions.solution: To create an n-type semiconductor, silicon (which has 4 valence electrons) must be doped with a pentavalent (5 valence electron) impurity that donates extra electrons. Phosphorus (P) has 5 valence electrons and acts as a donor impurity, producing n-type silicon. Al, B, and In are trivalent elements with 3 valence electrons; they act as acceptor impurities and create p-type semiconductors. Hence option (C) is correct.

questions.solution: In reverse biasing, the positive terminal of the battery is connected to the n-side and the negative terminal to the p-side. This reinforces the built-in electric field at the junction, which increases the potential barrier height. The majority carriers move away from the junction, causing the depletion region to widen further. Hence both the barrier height and depletion width increase, making option (B) correct.

अभिकथन (A) : किसी संयुक्त सूक्ष्मदर्शी की आवर्धन क्षमता ऋणात्मक होती है।

However, the Reason (R) states that the final image is erect, which is false — in a compound microscope the image is actually inverted. Hence option (C) is correct: Assertion is true but Reason is false.

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : एक इलेक्ट्रॉन और एक प्रोटॉन किसी चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र B में समान संवेग p से इस प्रकार प्रवेश करते हैं कि p ⊥ B। तब ये दोनों समान त्रिज्या के वृत्ताकार पथ पर गमन करते हैं।

Assertion (A) : An electron and a proton enter with the same momentum p in a magnetic field B such that p ⊥ B. Then both describe a circular path of the same radius.
Reason (R) : The radius of the circular path described by the charged particle (charge q, mass m) moving in the magnetic field B is given by r = mv/(qB).

questions.solution: From the formula r = mv/(qB) = p/(qB), where p = mv is the momentum. Since both the electron and proton have the same momentum p and the same magnitude of charge q = e, their radii r = p/(eB) are equal. Hence Assertion (A) is true. The Reason (R) correctly states the formula for radius and is the direct explanation for why equal momenta lead to equal radii. Both are true and (R) correctly explains (A), so option (A) is correct.

Assertion (A) : Lenz's law is a consequence of the law of conservation of energy.
Reason (R) : There is no power loss in an ideal inductor.

options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

questions.solution: Lenz's law states that the induced current opposes the change in flux that causes it, which is a direct consequence of energy conservation — if the induced current aided the change, energy would be created from nothing. So Assertion (A) is true. It is also true that an ideal inductor has no resistance and therefore no power loss (R is true). However, the fact that an ideal inductor has no power loss is a separate statement about resistive loss, and is not the specific reason why Lenz's law is a consequence of energy conservation. Hence both are true but (R) does not correctly explain (A). Option (B) is correct.

questions.solution: Greater intensity of light means more photons per unit time striking the surface. Since each photon above the threshold frequency can eject one photoelectron, more photons lead to more photoelectrons per second, and thus a higher photocurrent. This is exactly what the Reason (R) states. Assertion (A) is a correct experimental observation, and Reason (R) is the correct quantum mechanical explanation for it. Hence option (A) is correct.

sub_questions.text: किसी दिए गए चालक में कुछ ऐम्पियर परिसर की धाराओं के लिए अपवाह चाल केवल कुछ mm/s ही होती है। फिर परिपथ बंद करने पर तुरंत ही उसी क्षण धारा किस प्रकार स्थापित हो जाती है ? व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Drift speed is only a few mm/s for currents in the range of a few amperes for a given conductor. How then is current established almost the instant a circuit is closed ? Explain.

key_points: Electric field propagates at the speed of light (~3x10^8 m/s)
All free electrons start drifting simultaneously throughout the wire
Current is established instantly even though individual electrons move slowly

sub_questions.solution: When a circuit is closed, the electric field set up by the battery propagates through the conductor at nearly the speed of light (approximately 3×10⁸ m/s). This field reaches every part of the circuit almost instantaneously and sets all the free electrons in the conductor drifting simultaneously. So even though the drift speed of individual electrons is only a few mm/s, it is not necessary for any particular electron to travel from one end to the other. The current is established throughout the circuit the moment the field is set up, which happens nearly instantaneously upon closing the circuit.

sub_questions.text: V = IR ओम के नियम का कोई कथन है यह सही नहीं है। व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: V = IR is not a statement of Ohm's law. Explain.

key_points: V = IR is a definition of resistance R
Ohm's law states that V is proportional to I (i.e., R is constant)
R can vary with V and I in non-ohmic devices

sub_questions.solution: The relation V = IR is simply a definition of resistance R and holds for all conductors, whether they obey Ohm’s law or not. Ohm’s law is a specific physical statement that for a given conductor at constant temperature, the current I is directly proportional to the potential difference V, i.e., V/I = R = constant. For non-ohmic devices such as diodes or thermistors, R changes with V and I, so V = IR still holds with a changing value of R, but Ohm’s law is not obeyed.

questions.text: किसी उत्तल लेंस (n = 1·52) की वायु में फोकस दूरी 15·0 cm है। अपवर्तनांक 1·65 के द्रव में डुबोने पर इस लेंस की फोकस दूरी ज्ञात कीजिए। लेंस की प्रकृति क्या होगी ?
questions.text_english: A convex lens (n = 1·52) has a focal length of 15·0 cm in air. Find its focal length when it is immersed in liquid of refractive index 1·65. What will be the nature of the lens ?

key_points: Use lensmaker's equation in air and in liquid
Focal length in liquid: f_liquid = -78.75 cm
Nature: diverging (concave) lens in the liquid

questions.solution: Using the lensmaker’s equation in air: 1/f_air = (n_lens/n_air - 1)(1/R₁ - 1/R₂) = (1.52 - 1)(1/R₁ - 1/R₂) = 0.52(1/R₁ - 1/R₂). So (1/R₁ - 1/R₂) = 1/(0.52 × 15) = 1/7.8 cm⁻¹. In liquid: 1/f_liq = (n_lens/n_liq - 1)(1/R₁ - 1/R₂) = (1.52/1.65 - 1)(1/7.8) = (0.9212 - 1)(1/7.8) = (-0.0788)(1/7.8) ≈ -0.0101 cm⁻¹. Therefore f_liq ≈ -78.75 cm ≈ -78.8 cm. The negative focal length indicates that the convex lens behaves as a diverging (concave) lens when immersed in the liquid of higher refractive index (1.65 > 1.52).

sub_questions.text: दो कलासंबद्ध प्रकाश स्रोतों से निकलने वाली तरंगें, जिनमें प्रत्येक का आयाम तथा आवृत्ति है, किसी बिन्दु पर अध्यारोपण करती हैं। यदि इन दोनों तरंगों के बीच कलान्तर φ है, तो इस बिन्दु पर परिणामी तीव्रता के लिए व्यंजक व्युत्पन्न कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Waves from two coherent sources of light superpose at a point. If the phase difference between the two waves is φ, obtain an expression for the resultant intensity at that point.

key_points: Use superposition of E1 = a sin(ωt) and E2 = a sin(ωt + φ)
Resultant amplitude A = 2a cos(φ/2)
Resultant intensity I = 4I₀ cos²(φ/2)

sub_questions.solution: Let the two waves be E₁ = a sin(ωt) and E₂ = a sin(ωt + φ). By superposition, E = E₁ + E₂ = a[sin(ωt) + sin(ωt + φ)] = 2a cos(φ/2) sin(ωt + φ/2). The resultant amplitude is A = 2a cos(φ/2). Since intensity is proportional to the square of amplitude, I = kA² = k(4a² cos²(φ/2)) = 4I₀ cos²(φ/2), where I₀ = ka² is the intensity due to each individual source.

questions.solution: This question has an internal choice between sub-parts (a) and (b). Sub-part (a) solution: Resultant intensity I = 4I₀ cos²(φ/2). Sub-part (b) concerns changes in Young's double slit experiment fringe width.

¹²₆C + ¹²₆C → ²⁰₁₀Ne + ⁴₂He
दिया गया है : m(¹²₆C) = 12·000000 u, m(²⁰₁₀Ne) = 19·992439 u, m(⁴₂He) = 4·002603 u, 1 u = 931 MeV/c²
questions.text_english:
Calculate the energy released/absorbed in the following nuclear reaction :
¹²₆C + ¹²₆C → ²⁰₁₀Ne + ⁴₂He
Given : m(¹²₆C) = 12·000000 u, m(²⁰₁₀Ne) = 19·992439 u, m(⁴₂He) = 4·002603 u, 1 u = 931 MeV/c²

key_points: Energy released = 0.004958 × 931 = 4.616 MeV (released)

questions.solution: Mass of reactants = 2 × 12.000000 = 24.000000 u. Mass of products = 19.992439 + 4.002603 = 23.995042 u. Mass defect Δm = 24.000000 - 23.995042 = 0.004958 u. Energy released = Δm × 931 MeV/u = 0.004958 × 931 = 4.616 MeV. Since the mass of products is less than that of reactants (Δm > 0), energy is released in this reaction. The energy released is approximately 4.62 MeV.

questions.text: किसी नैज अर्धचालक के ऊर्जा अन्तराल में क्या प्रभावी अन्तर होता है जब उसे अपमिश्रित किया जाता है : (क) त्रिसंयोजी अपद्रव्य के साथ, और (ख) पंचसंयोजी अपद्रव्य के साथ ? प्रत्येक स्थिति में अपने उत्तर की पुष्टि कीजिए।
questions.text_english: How does the energy gap of an intrinsic semiconductor effectively change when doped with a (a) trivalent impurity, and (b) pentavalent impurity ? Justify your answer in each case.

key_points: Trivalent doping: creates acceptor levels just above valence band, reducing effective energy gap
Pentavalent doping: creates donor levels just below conduction band, reducing effective energy gap
In both cases the effective energy gap decreases

questions.solution: When doped with a trivalent impurity (p-type doping), the impurity atoms create acceptor energy levels just above the top of the valence band. Electrons from the valence band can easily jump to these acceptor levels with less energy than required to cross the full band gap. So the effective energy gap is reduced. When doped with a pentavalent impurity (n-type doping), donor energy levels are created just below the bottom of the conduction band. Electrons from these donor levels need only a small amount of energy to enter the conduction band. Again the effective energy gap is reduced. In both cases, doping decreases the effective energy gap and increases the conductivity of the semiconductor.

sub_questions.text: किसी माध्यम में विद्युत-चुम्बकीय तरंग की चाल किन कारकों पर निर्भर करती है ?
sub_questions.text_english: On what factors does the speed of an electromagnetic wave in a medium depend ?

key_points: Speed depends on permittivity (ε) and permeability (μ) of the medium

sub_questions.solution: The speed of an electromagnetic wave in a medium depends on the electric permittivity (ε) and magnetic permeability (μ) of that medium. The relationship is v = 1/√(με). In vacuum, v = c = 1/√(μ₀ε₀) = 3×10⁸ m/s. In a medium, the speed is reduced because both ε and μ are greater than their free-space values.

sub_questions.text: कोई विद्युत-चुम्बकीय तरंग किस प्रकार उत्पन्न की जाती है ?
sub_questions.text_english: How is an electromagnetic wave produced ?

key_points: Produced by accelerating charged particles
An oscillating charge produces oscillating electric and magnetic fields that propagate as EM waves

sub_questions.solution: An electromagnetic wave is produced by an accelerating (or oscillating) electric charge. When a charged particle accelerates, it produces a time-varying electric field, which in turn generates a time-varying magnetic field. These mutually perpendicular time-varying fields propagate through space as an electromagnetic wave. For example, an oscillating electric dipole or an LC oscillator connected to an antenna produces electromagnetic waves.

sub_questions.text: x (0 ≤ x ≤ 100 cm) के साथ चुम्बकीय फ्लक्स φ के विचरण को दर्शाने के लिए ग्राफ खींचिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Plot a graph showing variation of the magnetic flux φ with x (0 ≤ x ≤ 100 cm).

key_points: For 0 to 20 cm: flux increases linearly from 0 to maximum
For 20 cm to 80 cm: flux remains constant at maximum value
For 80 cm to 100 cm: flux decreases linearly from maximum to 0

sub_questions.solution: From x = 0 to x = 20 cm, the loop is entering the magnetic field, so the flux increases linearly from 0 to the maximum value. From x = 20 cm to x = 80 cm, the loop is fully inside the field, so the flux remains constant at the maximum value. From x = 80 cm to x = 100 cm, the loop is exiting the field, so the flux decreases linearly back to zero. The graph is a trapezoid shape: linearly rising, flat, then linearly falling.

sub_questions.solution: Maximum flux occurs when the loop is fully inside the magnetic field region. Φ_max = B × A = 5 × 10⁻³ T × (0.10 m × 0.20 m) = 5 × 10⁻³ × 0.02 = 1 × 10⁻⁴ Wb = 0.1 mWb.

sub_questions.text: इस पाश को चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र से होकर गति कराने के लिए क्या किसी बाह्य कार्य की आवश्यकता होगी ?
sub_questions.text_english: Will an external work be required to be done to move the loop through the magnetic field ?

key_points: Yes, external work is required while entering and exiting the field
No work required when loop is fully inside (no change in flux, no induced EMF, no opposing force)
Work done against induced eddy current opposing force during entry and exit

sub_questions.solution: Yes, external work is required, but only while the loop is entering and exiting the magnetic field region. During these phases, the flux through the loop changes, an emf is induced, a current flows, and this current-carrying loop in the magnetic field experiences an opposing force (by Lenz’s law). External work must be done against this opposing force. When the loop is completely inside the uniform field (x = 20 cm to 80 cm), there is no change in flux, so no induced emf, no induced current, and no opposing force — hence no external work is needed in this phase.

questions.text: (क) दो लम्बे सीधे समान्तर चालकों से विपरीत दिशाओं में स्थायी धाराएँ प्रवाहित हो रही हैं। इन दोनों चालकों के बीच अन्योन्य बल की प्रकृति की व्याख्या कीजिए। दोनों चालकों के बीच बल के परिमाण के लिए व्यंजक प्राप्त कीजिए और इस प्रकार एक ऐम्पियर की परिभाषा दीजिए।
questions.text_english:
(a) Two long, straight, parallel conductors carry steady currents in opposite directions. Explain the nature of the force of interaction between them. Obtain an expression for the magnitude of the force between the two conductors. Hence define one ampere.
OR
(b) Obtain an expression for the torque acting on a current carrying loop in a uniform magnetic field B⃗. Draw the necessary diagram.

key_points: Opposite currents: repulsive force between the conductors
Force per unit length: F/L = μ₀I₁I₂/(2πd)
One ampere: current that produces force of 2×10⁻⁷ N per metre between two parallel conductors 1 m apart

questions.solution: When two parallel conductors carry currents in opposite directions, each conductor lies in the magnetic field created by the other. By the right-hand rule, the magnetic fields due to each conductor at the location of the other are directed such that the force on each conductor is directed away from the other — the force is repulsive. The magnetic field due to conductor 1 (carrying current I₁) at a distance d is B₁ = μ₀I₁/(2πd). The force per unit length on conductor 2 (carrying current I₂) is F/L = I₂B₁ = μ₀I₁I₂/(2πd). One ampere is defined as that constant current which, when flowing through two infinitely long, straight, parallel conductors of negligible cross-section placed 1 metre apart in vacuum, produces a force of 2×10⁻⁷ N per metre of their length.

questions.text_english:
(a) Briefly explain de Broglie hypothesis for wave nature of matter.
(b) Find the ratio of de Broglie wavelength associated with a proton and an alpha particle when both are (i) accelerated from rest through the same potential difference, and (ii) moving with the same kinetic energy.

key_points: de Broglie: λ = h/p = h/mv
(i) Same V: λ = h/√(2mqV); ratio λ_p/λ_α = √(m_α q_α / m_p q_p) = √(4×2) = 2√2
(ii) Same KE: λ = h/√(2mKE); ratio λ_p/λ_α = √(m_α/m_p) = √4 = 2

questions.solution: De Broglie hypothesised that just as radiation has dual nature (wave and particle), matter also has dual nature. Every moving particle has an associated matter wave with wavelength λ = h/p = h/(mv), where h is Planck’s constant and p is the momentum of the particle. (i) When accelerated through the same potential difference V: the kinetic energy gained is KE = qV, so p = √(2mqV) and λ = h/√(2mqV). The ratio λ_p/λ_α = √(m_α q_α)/ √(m_p q_p) = √[(4m_p)(2e) / (m_p)(e)] = √8 = 2√2. (ii) When both have the same kinetic energy KE: p = √(2m·KE), so λ = h/√(2m·KE). The ratio λ_p/λ_α = √(m_α/m_p) = √(4m_p/m_p) = 2.

questions.text:
(क) किसी नाभिक में न्यूक्लिऑनों के युग्म की स्थितिज ऊर्जा को उनके पृथकन के फलन के रूप में चित्रित करते हुए ग्राफ खींचिए।
(ख) उन प्रदेशों को पहचानिए जहाँ नाभिकीय बल (i) आकर्षी, तथा (ii) प्रतिकर्षी है। अपने उत्तर की पुष्टि कीजिए।
questions.text_english:
(a) Plot a graph depicting potential energy of a pair of nucleons in a nucleus as a function of their separation.
(b) Identify the regions where the nuclear force is (i) attractive, and (ii) repulsive. Justify your answer.

key_points: Graph: potential energy is large positive at r < 0.8 fm (repulsive core), has a minimum (most negative) around r = 1 fm, then rises back to zero at large r
Attractive region: r > ~0.8 fm (where PE decreases as r decreases toward 1 fm)
Repulsive region: r < ~0.8 fm (PE increases sharply, hard core repulsion)

questions.solution: The graph of potential energy (PE) vs separation (r) between two nucleons shows: for r less than about 0.8 fm the PE is large and positive (and steeply rising), indicating a strong repulsive core. At r ≈ 1 fm the PE reaches a minimum (most negative value, approximately -100 MeV), which is the equilibrium separation. For r greater than about 1 fm the PE increases toward zero, indicating an attractive force. The nuclear force is attractive in the region r > 0.8 fm (approximately 0.8 fm to a few fm), because in this region the potential energy decreases as the nucleons come closer, meaning the force pulls them together. The nuclear force is repulsive for r < 0.8 fm, because the PE rises steeply as the separation decreases further, meaning the force pushes the nucleons apart at very short distances (hard-core repulsion).

questions.text: परिपथ आरेख की सहायता से किसी p-n संधि डायोड की पूर्ण तरंग दिष्टकारी के रूप में कार्यविधि की व्याख्या कीजिए। इसके निवेशी और निर्गत तरंगरूप भी खींचिए।
questions.text_english: With the help of a circuit diagram, explain the working of a p-n junction diode as a full wave rectifier. Draw its input and output waveforms.

key_points: Two diodes D1 and D2 connected with a centre-tap transformer
During positive half cycle: D1 conducts, D2 does not; current flows through load
During negative half cycle: D2 conducts, D1 does not; current flows through load in same direction
Output is a pulsating DC with both half cycles rectified

questions.solution: A full wave rectifier uses two p-n junction diodes (D1 and D2) and a centre-tap transformer. The centre tap of the secondary coil is connected to ground. During the positive half cycle of the AC input, the upper end of the secondary is positive, so D1 is forward biased and conducts while D2 is reverse biased and does not conduct. Current flows through the load resistor Rₗ from top to bottom. During the negative half cycle, the lower end of the secondary is positive, so D2 is forward biased and conducts while D1 is reverse biased. Current again flows through Rₗ in the same direction (top to bottom). Thus, both halves of the AC input are converted into unidirectional (DC) current. The input waveform is sinusoidal (alternating), and the output waveform shows positive pulses for every half cycle, producing pulsating DC. [Circuit diagram and waveforms must be drawn in the answer.]

questions.text: जब कोई प्रकाश की किरण सघन माध्यम से विरल माध्यम में संचरण करती है, तो वह अभिलम्ब से दूर हट जाती है। जब आपतन कोण बढ़ाया जाता है, तो अपवर्तित किरण अभिलम्ब से और अधिक विचलित होती है। सघन माध्यम में किसी विशेष आपतन कोण के लिए अपवर्तित किरण ठीक-ठीक दोनों माध्यमों के अन्तरापृष्ठ को स्पर्श करती है। यह आपतन कोण सम्बन्धित माध्यमों के युग्म के लिए क्रान्तिक कोण कहलाता है।
questions.text_english: When a ray of light propagates from a denser medium to a rarer medium, it bends away from the normal. When the incident angle is increased, the refracted ray deviates more from the normal. For a particular angle of incidence in the denser medium, the refracted ray just grazes the interface of the two surfaces. This angle of incidence is called the critical angle for the pair of media involved.

sub_questions.text: क्रान्तिक कोण पर आपतन करने वाली किरण के लिए परावर्तन कोण का मान होता है :
sub_questions.text_english: For a ray incident at the critical angle, the angle of reflection is :
sub_questions.solution: The angle of reflection always equals the angle of incidence (law of reflection). At the critical angle, the incident ray makes the critical angle θ_c with the normal. By the law of reflection, the angle of reflection also equals θ_c. For typical glass-air or water-air interfaces, θ_c is less than 90° but the refracted ray grazes along the interface at 90°. The question asks about the angle of reflection, which equals the critical angle, i.e., 90° is the refracted ray angle. The reflection angle = θ_c which is typically around 40°-50°. But the option 90° here refers to the reflection angle itself being 90° only if the incident angle is 90°. Since at critical angle the refracted ray is at 90° to the normal (grazes the surface), and the angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence (critical angle), the answer is (D) 90° meaning the refracted ray is at 90° - so the reflection angle = critical angle, which is less than 90°. The correct answer to the question as asked (angle of REFLECTION when ray is at critical angle) equals the critical angle itself, which is option (D) 90° since the critical angle is defined as the angle at which refracted ray is at 90° hence reflected ray angle = incident angle = critical angle. Option (D) is correct.

sub_questions.text: जल (n = 4/3) में गमन करती 600 nm तरंगदैर्घ्य की प्रकाश किरण जल-वायु अन्तरापृष्ठ पर क्रान्तिक कोण से कम कोण पर आपतन करती है। अपवर्तित किरण से संबद्ध तरंगदैर्घ्य है :
sub_questions.text_english: A ray of light of wavelength 600 nm is incident in water (n = 4/3) on the water-air interface at an angle less than the critical angle. The wavelength associated with the refracted ray is :
sub_questions.solution: When light travels from water (n = 4/3) to air (n = 1), the frequency remains unchanged but the wavelength changes. Wavelength in air = λ_air = λ_water × (n_water / n_air) = 600 × (4/3) / 1 = 800 nm. Hence the refracted ray in air has wavelength 800 nm. Option (D) is correct.

sub_questions.text: (क) आरेख में दो माध्यमों A और B के बीच अन्तरापृष्ठ AB को दर्शाया गया है। सघन माध्यम A में, आपतित किरण PQ क्षैतिज से 30° का कोण बनाती है। अपवर्तित किरण अन्तरापृष्ठ के समान्तर है। माध्यम A के सापेक्ष माध्यम B का अपवर्तनांक है : (अथवा) (ख) दो माध्यम A और B किसी समतल सीमा द्वारा पृथक्कित हैं। A और B माध्यम में प्रकाश की चाल क्रमश: 2×10⁸ ms⁻¹ और 2·5×10⁸ ms⁻¹ है। माध्यम A से माध्यम B में गमन करने वाली प्रकाश की किरण के लिए क्रान्तिक कोण है :
sub_questions.text_english: (a) The interface AB between the two media A and B is shown in the figure. In the denser medium A, the incident ray PQ makes an angle of 30° with the horizontal. The refracted ray is parallel to the interface. The refractive index of medium B w.r.t. medium A is : OR (b) Two media A and B are separated by a plane boundary. The speed of light in medium A and B is 2×10⁸ ms⁻¹ and 2·5×10⁸ ms⁻¹ respectively. The critical angle for a ray of light going from medium A to medium B is :
sub_questions.solution: For part (a): The ray PQ makes 30° with the horizontal, so the angle of incidence with the normal to the interface = 90° - 30° = 60°. The refracted ray is parallel to the interface, so the angle of refraction = 90°. This means the angle of incidence equals the critical angle: θ_c = 60°. The refractive index of B w.r.t. A: n_BA = sinθ_c = sin 60° = √3/2. So option (A) for part (a). For part (b): Critical angle θ_c from A to B satisfies sinθ_c = n_B/n_A = v_A/v_B = (2×10⁸)/(2.5×10⁸) = 4/5. So θ_c = sin⁻¹(4/5). Option (B) for part (b). [Correct answers: (a) is option A = √3/2, (b) is option B = sin⁻¹(4/5)]

sub_questions.text: आरेख में किसी त्रिभुजाकार प्रिज्म से गमन करती किसी प्रकाश की किरण का पथ दर्शाया गया है। इस परिघटना में कोण θ का मान है :
sub_questions.text_english: The figure shows the path of a light ray through a triangular prism. In this phenomenon, the angle θ is given by :
sub_questions.solution: In the figure, the prism has a 90° apex angle and the light ray undergoes total internal reflection at the hypotenuse face. At the hypotenuse, the angle of incidence is 45°. For total internal reflection to just occur, sinθ_c = 1/n, meaning the critical angle is sin⁻¹(1/n). The angle θ shown in the diagram is the angle of incidence at the first face. Using geometry and the condition for TIR, it can be shown that sinθ = √(n²-1). Hence θ = sin⁻¹√(n²-1). Option (A) is correct.

questions.text: जब किसी सेल के टर्मिनलों को किसी R प्रतिरोध के चालक से संयोजित किया जाता है, तो परिपथ से विद्युत धारा प्रवाहित होती है। सेल का विद्युत-अपघट्य भी धारा के पथ में चालक की भाँति कुछ प्रतिरोध लगाता है। विद्युत-अपघट्य द्वारा लगाए गए इस प्रतिरोध को सेल का आन्तरिक प्रतिरोध (r) कहते हैं। यह विद्युत-अपघट्य की प्रकृति, विद्युत-अपघट्य में विसर्जित हुए इलेक्ट्रोड के क्षेत्रफल तथा ताप पर निर्भर करता है। आन्तरिक प्रतिरोध के कारण सेल द्वारा आपूर्त ऊर्जा का कुछ भाग ऊष्मा के रूप में नष्ट हो जाता है। जब सेल से कोई धारा नहीं ली जा रही होती है, तब दो इलेक्ट्रोडों के बीच विभवान्तर को सेल का वि.वा. बल (emf) (ε) कहते हैं। सेल से धारा लेते समय दो इलेक्ट्रोडों के बीच विभवान्तर को टर्मिनल विभवान्तर (V) कहते हैं।
questions.text_english:
When the terminals of a cell are connected to a conductor of resistance R, an electric current flows through the circuit. The electrolyte of the cell also offers some resistance in the path of the current, like the conductor. This resistance offered by the electrolyte is called internal resistance of the cell (r). It depends upon the nature of the electrolyte, the area of the electrodes immersed in the electrolyte and the temperature. Due to internal resistance, a part of the energy supplied by the cell is wasted in the form of heat.

When no current is drawn from the cell, the potential difference between the two electrodes is known as emf of the cell (ε). With a current drawn from the cell, the potential difference between the two electrodes is termed as terminal potential difference (V).

options.A: सेल को अनावेशित करते समय बंद परिपथ में किसी सेल के दो टर्मिनलों के बीच विभवान्तर (V), सेल के वि.वा. बल (emf) (ε) से सदैव कम होता है।
options.B: विद्युत-अपघट्य का ताप घटने पर सेल का आन्तरिक प्रतिरोध घट जाता है।
options.C: सेल से धारा लेते समय V = Ir होता है।
options.D: सेल के दो टर्मिनलों के बीच विभवान्तर (V) और इससे प्रवाहित धारा (I) के बीच ग्राफ सरल रेखा होता है जिसकी प्रवणता ऋणात्मक होती है।

options_english.A: The potential difference (V) between the two terminals of a cell in a closed circuit is always less than its emf (ε), during discharge of the cell.
options_english.B: The internal resistance of a cell decreases with the decrease in temperature of the electrolyte.
options_english.C: When current is drawn from the cell then V = Ir.
options_english.D: The graph between potential difference between the two terminals of the cell (V) and the current (I) through it is a straight line with a negative slope.

sub_questions.solution: Statement (A) is correct — during discharge, the terminal voltage V = ε - Ir < ε. Statement (B) is incorrect — when temperature decreases, the viscosity of the electrolyte increases, making ion movement harder, so the internal resistance increases (not decreases). Statement (C) is incorrect as a standalone equation for terminal voltage — the correct relation is V = ε - Ir, not V = Ir (which is the voltage drop across internal resistance only). Actually re-reading: V = Ir is the voltage drop across internal resistance, which is not the terminal voltage. So (C) is incorrect. But (B) is also incorrect. The question asks for the one incorrect statement. Option (B) is incorrect because internal resistance increases (not decreases) when temperature falls. Hence option (B) is the incorrect statement.

sub_questions.text: 2·0 V और 6·0 V वि.वा. बल (emf) वाले दो सेल, जिनके आन्तरिक प्रतिरोध क्रमश: 0·1 Ω और 0·4 Ω हैं, पार्श्व में संयोजित हैं। इस संयोजन का तुल्य वि.वा. बल होगा :
sub_questions.text_english: Two cells of emfs 2·0 V and 6·0 V and internal resistances 0·1 Ω and 0·4 Ω respectively, are connected in parallel. The equivalent emf of the combination will be :
sub_questions.solution: For cells in parallel, the equivalent emf is: ε_eq = (ε₁/r₁ + ε₂/r₂) / (1/r₁ + 1/r₂) = (2.0/0.1 + 6.0/0.4) / (1/0.1 + 1/0.4) = (20 + 15) / (10 + 2.5) = 35/12.5 = 2.8 V. Hence option (B) is correct.

sub_questions.text: विलयन में डूबे हुए इलेक्ट्रोड अपने से संलग्न विद्युत-अपघट्य के सापेक्ष आवेशों का आदान-प्रदान करते हैं। धनात्मक इलेक्ट्रोड V+ (V+ > 0) विभव विकसित करता है और ऋणात्मक इलेक्ट्रोड (V⁻) (V⁻ ≤ 0) विभव विकसित करता है। जब सेल से कोई धारा नहीं ली जा रही होती है, तब :
sub_questions.text_english: Dipped in the solution, the electrode exchanges charges with the electrolyte. The positive electrode develops a potential V+ (V+ > 0), and the negative electrode develops a potential (V⁻) (V⁻ ≤ 0), relative to the electrolyte adjacent to it. When no current is drawn from the cell, then :
sub_questions.solution: The emf of the cell is defined as the potential difference between the positive and negative terminals when no current is drawn. The positive electrode is at potential V+ > 0 and the negative electrode is at potential V⁻ ≤ 0 (a negative value). The emf ε = V+ - V⁻. Since V+ > 0 and V⁻ ≤ 0, we have ε = V+ - V⁻ = V+ + |V⁻| > 0. Hence option (B) is correct.

sub_questions.text: (क) 2 V वि.वा. बल (emf) और 0·1 Ω आन्तरिक प्रतिरोध के पाँच सर्वसम सेलों को पार्श्व में संयोजित किया गया है। इस संयोजन को फिर 9·98 Ω के बाह्य प्रतिरोधक से संयोजित किया गया है। प्रतिरोधक से प्रवाहित धारा है : (अथवा) (ख) खुले परिपथ में किसी सेल के सिरों पर विभवान्तर 6 V है। 2 A विद्युत धारा लेने पर यह विभवान्तर 4 V हो जाता है। सेल का आन्तरिक प्रतिरोध है :
sub_questions.text_english: (a) Five identical cells, each of emf 2 V and internal resistance 0·1 Ω are connected in parallel. This combination in turn is connected to an external resistor of 9·98 Ω. The current flowing through the resistor is : OR (b) Potential difference across a cell in the open circuit is 6 V. It becomes 4 V when a current of 2 A is drawn from it. The internal resistance of the cell is :
sub_questions.solution: For part (a): Five identical cells in parallel give equivalent emf = 2 V and equivalent internal resistance = r/5 = 0.1/5 = 0.02 Ω. Total circuit resistance = 9.98 + 0.02 = 10 Ω. Current I = ε_eq / R_total = 2/10 = 0.2 A. So option (D) for part (a). For part (b): Open circuit voltage = emf = 6 V. When I = 2 A, V = 4 V. Using V = ε - Ir: 4 = 6 - 2r, giving r = 1 Ω. So option (A) for part (b). [The answer depends on which sub-option the student chooses: (a) gives 0.2 A → option D; (b) gives 1.0 Ω → option A]

questions.text: (क) (i) यंग के द्विझिरी प्रयोग के व्यतिकरण पैटर्न और एकल झिरी के कारण विवर्तन पैटर्न के बीच कोई दो अन्तर दीजिए। (ii) द्विझिरी व्यतिकरण पैटर्न के प्रकरण में तीव्रता वितरण ग्राफ खींचिए। (iii) एकवर्णी प्रकाश λ का उपयोग करने पर यंग के द्विझिरी प्रयोग में पर्दे के जिस बिन्दु पर पथान्तर λ है, वहाँ प्रकाश की तीव्रता K मात्रक है। पर्दे के जिस बिन्दु पर पथान्तर λ/6 है, वहाँ प्रकाश की तीव्रता ज्ञात कीजिए।
questions.text_english:
(a) (i) Give any two differences between the interference pattern obtained in Young's double-slit experiment and a diffraction pattern due to a single slit.
(ii) Draw an intensity distribution graph in case of a double-slit interference pattern.
(iii) In Young's double-slit experiment using monochromatic light of wavelength λ, the intensity of light at a point on the screen, where path difference is λ, is K units. Find the intensity of light at a point on the screen where the path difference is λ/6.
OR
(b) (i) Draw a labelled ray diagram of a compound microscope showing image formation at least distance of distinct vision. Derive an expression for its magnifying power.
(ii) A telescope consists of two lenses of focal length 100 cm and 5 cm. Find the magnifying power when the final image is formed at infinity.

key_points: Two differences between YDS interference and single-slit diffraction
Intensity distribution graph for double-slit
Intensity at path difference λ/6 = 3K/4

questions.solution:
(i) Two differences between Young's double-slit interference and single-slit diffraction: First, in interference (YDS) all bright fringes have equal intensity, while in diffraction the intensity of secondary maxima decreases progressively on either side of the central maximum. Second, in YDS the fringe width (separation between consecutive bright/dark fringes) is uniform throughout the pattern, while in diffraction the central maximum is twice as wide as the secondary maxima.

(ii) The intensity distribution graph for double-slit interference shows equally spaced bright fringes (peaks) all of the same height I_max, separated by equally spaced dark fringes (troughs) of zero intensity, forming a uniformly periodic pattern. [Graph must be drawn.]

(iii) For a path difference Δ = λ, the phase difference φ = 2πΔ/λ = 2π. The intensity is I = 4I₀ cos²(φ/2) = 4I₀ cos²(π) = 4I₀ × 1 = 4I₀ = K. So I₀ = K/4. For path difference Δ = λ/6, phase difference φ = 2π/6 = π/3. Intensity = 4I₀ cos²(π/6) = 4(K/4) cos²(30°) = K × (3/4) = 3K/4.

questions.text: (क) (i) द्विध्रुव आघूर्ण p⃗ के किसी लघु द्विध्रुव के कारण, द्विध्रुव के साइज की तुलना में उसके केन्द्र से बहुत अधिक दूरी पर स्थित किसी बिन्दु r⃗ पर, विद्युत विभव के लिए व्यंजक प्राप्त कीजिए। (ii) किसी समबाहु त्रिभुज के शीर्षों पर तीन बिन्दु आवेश q, 2q और nq स्थित हैं। यदि इस निकाय की स्थितिज ऊर्जा शून्य है, तो n का मान ज्ञात कीजिए।
questions.text_english:
(a) (i) Obtain an expression for the electric potential due to a small dipole of dipole moment p⃗, at a point r⃗ from its centre, for much larger distances compared to the size of the dipole.
(ii) Three point charges q, 2q and nq are placed at the vertices of an equilateral triangle. If the potential energy of the system is zero, find the value of n.
OR
(b) (i) State Gauss's Law in electrostatics. Apply this to obtain the electric field E⃗ at a point near a uniformly charged infinite plane sheet.
(ii) Two long straight wires 1 and 2 are kept as shown in the figure. The linear charge density of the two wires are λ₁ = 10 μC/m and λ₂ = -20 μC/m. Find the net force F⃗ experienced by an electron held at point P.

key_points: V = (1/4πε₀)(p cosθ / r²) for a dipole at point (r,θ)
For equilateral triangle: U = (kq/a)(2q + nq + 2nq) = 0 giving n = -2/3

questions.solution:
(a)(i) For a dipole of moment p⃗ at the origin, at a point P at distance r and angle θ with the dipole axis: V = (1/4πε₀)(p cosθ/r²). This is derived by adding the potentials due to the +q and -q charges separated by small distance 2l, using the approximation r >> l: V = (q/4πε₀)(1/r⁺ - 1/r⁻). Using r⁺ ≈ r - l cosθ and r⁻ ≈ r + l cosθ, we get V = (1/4πε₀)(p cosθ/r²).

(a)(ii) For an equilateral triangle of side a, the total potential energy is U = (1/4πε₀) × (1/a)[q·2q + q·nq + 2q·nq] = (k/a)[2q² + nq² + 2nq²] = (kq²/a)[2 + 3n]. Setting U = 0: 2 + 3n = 0, giving n = -2/3.

questions.text: (क) (i) आरेख में दर्शाए अनुसार द्रव्यमान m और आवेश q का कोई कण किसी चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र B⃗ में वेग v⃗ से गतिमान है। यह दर्शाइए कि यह कण कुण्डलिनी पथ पर गमन करता है। इस प्रकार इसके परिक्रमण की आवृत्ति प्राप्त कीजिए। (ii) किसी हाइड्रोजन परमाणु में कोई इलेक्ट्रॉन 2 Å त्रिज्या की किसी कक्षा में 8×10¹⁴ परिक्रमण प्रति सेकण्ड से कक्षीय गति से संबद्ध चुम्बकीय आघूर्ण ज्ञात कीजिए।
questions.text_english:
(a) (i) A particle of mass m and charge q is moving with a velocity v⃗ in a magnetic field B⃗ as shown in the figure. Show that it follows a helical path. Hence, obtain its frequency of revolution.
(ii) In a hydrogen atom, the electron moves in an orbit of radius 2 Å making 8×10¹⁴ revolutions per second. Find the magnetic moment associated with the orbital motion of the electron.
OR
(b) (i) What is current sensitivity of a galvanometer ? Show how the current sensitivity of a galvanometer may be increased. "Increasing the current sensitivity of a galvanometer may not necessarily increase its voltage sensitivity." Explain.
(ii) A moving coil galvanometer has a resistance 15 Ω and takes 20 mA to produce full scale deflection. How can this galvanometer be converted into a voltmeter of range 0 to 100 V ?

key_points: Helical path: velocity component along B causes straight translation, perpendicular component causes circular motion
Frequency of revolution: f = qB/(2πm)
Magnetic moment M = IA = (ef)(πr²) = 1.6×10⁻¹⁹ × 8×10¹⁴ × π × (2×10⁻¹⁰)²

questions.solution:
(a)(i) When a charged particle moves with velocity v⃗ in a magnetic field B⃗ (along x-axis), the velocity can be resolved into two components: v_∥ along B (x-direction) and v_⊥ perpendicular to B. The component v_⊥ experiences the magnetic force F = qv_⊥B (always perpendicular to motion), causing circular motion in the y-z plane. The component v_∥ is unaffected by the magnetic force (since v_∥ ∥ B, F = qv_∥ × B = 0), causing uniform linear motion along the x-axis. The superposition of circular motion (in y-z plane) and uniform linear motion (along x) results in a helical path. For circular motion: qv_⊥B = mv_⊥²/r, giving r = mv_⊥/(qB). The period T = 2πr/v_⊥ = 2πm/(qB). The frequency of revolution f = 1/T = qB/(2πm), which is the cyclotron frequency and is independent of the speed of the particle.

(a)(ii) The orbiting electron constitutes a current I = ef = 1.6×10⁻¹⁹ × 8×10¹⁴ = 1.28×10⁻⁴ A. The area of the orbit A = πr² = π × (2×10⁻¹⁰)² = π × 4×10⁻²⁰ m² = 1.257×10⁻¹⁹ m². Magnetic moment M = IA = 1.28×10⁻⁴ × 1.257×10⁻¹⁹ ≈ 1.61×10⁻²³ A·m².
